hook: Two little dots turn 'I had' into 'I'd like', so train your ear to catch hätte, wäre and könnte every time.
intro: Fifteen sentences of wishes and requests in the Konjunktiv II, heard and typed. The ear must catch two things the eye finds easy. First, the umlaut: hätte/hatte, wäre/war, könnte/konnte, müsste/musste differ by one vowel — listen for the front vowel (ä, ö, ü) and write the dots, because 'Wenn ich Zeit hatte' is a different sentence. Second, the frame: würde or the one-word form in position 2, and the infinitive at the very end — Ich würde gern mehr reisen — so keep listening past the pause for the last word. In this dictation the umlauts are checked strictly, because they are the whole point: hatte for hätte is marked wrong, so type the dots.
tips[0].title: Hear the umlaut
tips[0].text: hätte (ä like 'bed'), wäre, könnte (ö — round the lips), müsste (ü — 'ee' with rounded lips). If you hear the front vowel, write the dots.
tips[0].check.why: An unreal 'if' needs the Konjunktiv hätte, with the ä. hatte is just the past tense, and hätten doesn't go with ich.
tips[1].title: The last word is the verb
tips[1].text: Ich würde gern mehr reisen. Könnten Sie mir bitte helfen? Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich kommen. Hold the sentence in your head to its end before typing.
tips[1].check.why: After würde the infinitive waits at the very end, so keep listening for that last word: besuchen.
tips[2].title: Comma before wenn-clause, comma after
tips[2].text: Wenn ich mehr Geld hätte, würde ich ein Auto kaufen. The pause after hätte is the comma; the verbs sit on either side of it.
tips[2].check.why: The comma sits between the two verbs: hätte ends the wenn-clause, würde opens the main clause.
remember[0]: ä ö ü: front vowel heard → dots written.
remember[1]: Verb at the end; comma at the pause.
exam: Spelling hätte, wäre and könnte correctly matters in every polite written request — in the B1 exam's writing tasks and in your own e-mails.
